claims.text: When a Pulumi program treats an Output as if it were a plain value (e.g., string interpolation), the placeholder text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` can appear in log lines, generated files, or resource properties instead of the expected value.

The Pulumi docs page 'Output value errors' at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers the `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` symptom and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
Treating an output as if it were already a plain value produces multiple distinct symptoms beyond the `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` placeholder text.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers diagnosing errors that result from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value as if it were a plain value.
Errors can arise in Pulumi programs from stringifying an output value, branching on an output value, or reading an output value as though it were a plain value.

Pulumi emits a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when a stack update conflicts with another in-progress update, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ covers resolving it.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/ covers handling them.
Pulumi can produce post-step event failures caused by engine bugs, covered at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/ exists and covers fixing network connectivity and proxy problems.

The Pulumi CLI reports `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, and the anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml exists on /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/.
`pulumi destroy` can fail, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ exists covering these scenarios.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/ exists and covers recovering from interrupted deployments.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause Pulumi crashes or hangs; the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/architecture-mismatch/ covers the fix.
The page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/ exists and covers resolving continuous integration and deployment pipeline issues.
The page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/ exists and describes safe techniques for modifying Pulumi state files.
A recently deleted Pulumi stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi CLI operations can be limited to specific resources with `--target` and `--exclude` flags.
Using targeted updates (`--target` and `--exclude`) can work around a stuck or misbehaving resource that is blocking a wider update.
The Pulumi logging documentation covers automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics.
Pulumi provides pre-release (dev) builds that can be installed to access bug fixes that have not yet shipped in a stable release.
Pulumi has a Community Slack (slack.pulumi.com) that offers community support.
A Pulumi guide for filing GitHub issues exists at /docs/support/filing-issues/ and explains how to report bugs in the right repository.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an `automatic-logging` anchor describing the automatic logging feature.
Pulumi offers paid support options, reachable via the /contact/ page.
Pulumi has a support page at /support/ where users can contact support.
GitHub issue pulumi/pulumi#20846 relates to the new update conflict page, and the #conflict hash on the troubleshooting page redirects to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/.
GitHub issue pulumi/docs#16985 relates to the new verbose logging page, and the #verbose-logging hash redirects to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging, an anchor that exists.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values, because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs exists and describes Outputs.
The Pulumi docs pages 'Accessing single outputs with Apply' (/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/) and 'Working with multiple outputs' (/docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/) exist.

When an output value is concatenated, logged, or otherwise converted to a string directly instead of via `apply` or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default and instead silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In Pulumi TypeScript, converting an Output to a string via a template literal produces a string containing the literal text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.

In Pulumi Python, formatting an Output into an f-string produces a string containing literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning; no exception is raised.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Pulumi Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the API to use to serialize an Output to JSON instead of `json.dumps()`.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error, not a runtime surprise.
In Pulumi Go, the fix is to resolve the value inside `ApplyT` and pass the result on.

In Pulumi C#, interpolating an Output into a string produces a string containing literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`; no exception is thrown.

Because the mistake produces a string rather than throwing, the program runs and `pulumi up` succeeds, with the placeholder text only surfacing later in log lines, generated config files, or downstream resource properties.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning the placeholder text.
The `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING` environment variable is supported in TypeScript, Python, and C# but not Go.
In Pulumi TypeScript, `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` are string-composition helpers for working with outputs.
In Pulumi Python, `Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` are string-composition helpers for working with outputs.
In Pulumi Go, `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` are helpers for string composition and JSON marshaling with outputs.
In Pulumi C#, `Output.Format` is the string-composition helper for working with outputs.

The value read out of an output inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in another output derived from it); assigning it to an outer variable and using it outside the callback does not work.

The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, which in general is after the rest of the program's top-level code has finished running, so reading an outer variable assigned in the callback yields `undefined`.
The `apply` callback runs when the Pulumi engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix reading the outer variable.
Passing an Output directly as a resource input (e.g. `bucket: bucket.bucketName` on `aws.s3.BucketObject`) works with no `apply` needed, and Pulumi resolves the dependency.
Most resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values.
A handful of positions cannot accept an output, such as a resource's logical name.
The page contains a section with anchor #using-an-output-as-a-resource-name-a-map-key-or-a-loop-bound.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on an output evaluates the output object itself rather than its eventual value, so it is generally always true regardless of what the output resolves to.
In a statically typed language, branching with `if` on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
A value known when the program starts, such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag, is a plain value and can be branched on directly.
When a branch depends on a resource's output, the branch has to move inside `apply`, with both outcomes expressed as values rather than program structure.

A runtime branch on an output cannot be expressed as separate blocks of resource-creation code, only as separate values, so the program typically must be restructured to describe both sets of resources unconditionally or branch on a plain config value.
A resource's logical name, loop bounds, and map keys used while authoring a program must be known plain values while the program is being evaluated, before any resource exists.
Passing an output as a resource's logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Pulumi Python, using an output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

When resource names or counts must depend on data only known after a resource has been created, a recommended fix is to provision the dependent resources in a later, separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/ has a `#stackreferences` anchor describing StackReference.
Trying to `await` an output or read its value synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or quietly returns placeholder text.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and pull a resolved value out of an output synchronously.

Synchronously reading an output's value is deliberately unsupported because it would defeat building the dependency graph up front, as the engine would need the value before determining the order to create resources.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A StackReference from another Pulumi program consumes one stack's outputs as another stack's inputs.
The Automation API's result of running an update has an `outputs` field (for example `res.Outputs` in Go) for reading stack outputs when driving deployments programmatically.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/ exists and documents the Automation API.
`pulumi stack output`, StackReference, and the Automation API outputs field all read a value that has already resolved rather than unwrapping an in-flight output from inside the same program.
